I opened the sidebar's _Views and More Actions..._ > _Views_ menu but the options to show the _Enabled_ and _Disabled_ views are missing.   Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.130.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 Home Version 25H2 OS build 26200.8875 --- Thanks for reporting this. In the fresh setup shown, there do not appear to be any disabled extensions. Please disable one installed extension, reopen **Views and More Actions... > Views**, and confirm whether the Enabled/Disabled view options then appear. title: Lost Chat
content:
Type: Bug I'm new to using VSC. Today is Day 0. I was in the middle of the setup / configuration steps when I clicked on the menu at the left of my screen to see what the icon would do. My prompt window disappeared and the only prompt window I could get back was blank. There was no history to be found anywhere using the icons and menus in the app. I turned to Perplexity and explained the issue. Perplexity guided me through the steps to see if I could find it and I discovered there might be a bug in the Mac version of the VSC app. When I click on the Explorer icon in the upper left corner of my screen on the menu side bar, the folder tree was completely blank. I had already gotten through the step that created a new folder structure on my computer and I could see that folder structure physically with contents inside some of the folders, but it wasn't appearing within the tree of the Explorer icon so the app treated it as if it didn't exist. I ended up recovering the work and picked up where I left off, by using a prompt in the VSC chat window. Here's my prompt: "I lost where we left off on the demo project. Please search my computer for the MD file and folder structure we created earlier today and pick up where we left off." Claude came back with a bunch of Bash commands which I had to approve, and was able to locate the information that was indeed, still available to the system and I was able to recover the work. It was all still there, but just not visible on the side bar menu. I have since been able to work to build that missing tree structure so I can come back later and find the same chat stream since I'm not finished with my project. title: Add Alt+click to close other tabs (JetBrains-style)
content: ## Feature Request Close all other tabs (except the current one) by _alt + clicking_ an editor tab's close button. By holding _alt_ over a tab's close button, the button swaps from the "Close" icon to a "Close Other Editors" icon. Clicking it closes all other tabs in the group, leaving the clicked tab open. **Note:** If there was an open sticky tab, it stays unchanged. This is the same behavior as JetBrains IDEs ([docs](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/mps/closing-files-in-the-editor.html)). ### Implementation PR: #328975 --- This is actually better than JetBrains, as their tooltip is static (doesn't change if _alt_ is pressed) and it shows the tips for both _Close_ and _Close Others_, making the tooltip polluted. Sharing media and context from merged PR #328975 for verification: # Add Alt+click to close other tabs (JetBrains-style) Close all other tabs (except the current one) by _alt + clicking_ an editor tab's close button. By holding _alt_ over an editor tab's close button, the button swaps from the "Close" icon to a "Close Other Editors" icon. Clicking it closes every other non-sticky tab in the group, leaving the clicked tab (and any sticky tabs) open. This is the same behavior as JetBrains IDEs ([docs](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/mps/closing-files-in-the-editor.html)). ## Demo ## Edge case: tabs whose `matches()` is intentionally loose Some editor inputs (e.g. `GettingStartedInput`, used for Welcome and walkthrough tabs) override `matches()` to return `true` for any instance of the same type, so VS Code can treat them as a reusable singleton pane elsewhere. Using `matches()` to decide what "close others" should close meant that if two such tabs were open together, alt + clicking one would incorrectly spare the other instead of closing it. The close filter compares by reference identity instead, since what matters here is "is this literally the tab that was clicked," not "is this the same kind of tab." ## Known limitation **Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR**, `workbench.action.closeOtherEditors` already has the identical exposure today. If two same type loosely-matching tabs (e.g. two `GettingStartedInput` tabs) are open in one group and the clicked tab is active, _closing others_ can close the wrong one. Needs a separate PR to fix it. ## How to test 1. Open several tabs (leave at least one pinned/sticky, if you'd like to check that case too) 2. Hover a non-sticky tab's close (×) button and hold _alt_: the icon swaps to "Close Other Editors" 3. Click it while _alt_ is held 4. Expect: every other non-sticky tab closes; sticky tabs and the clicked tab remain open 5. Release _alt_ without clicking: the icon reverts to the plain Close (×) 6. Hold _alt_ over a sticky tab's Unpin button: it should stay Unpin, unaffected by Alt ## Test coverage `multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` (real `MultiEditorTabsControl` + DOM + `EditorGroupModel`): - Shows Close by default, swaps to Close Other Editors while Alt is held, reverts on release - Sticky tabs keep showing Unpin regardless of Alt - Clicking while Alt is held closes every other non-sticky tab - Handles the `matches()` edge case above - Clicking a sticky tab's Unpin button while Alt is held does not close other tabs - Without Alt, clicking closes only that one tab `editorActions.test.ts` (`CloseOtherEditorTabsInGroupAction` in isolation): - Closes every other editor, keeping the target by reference - Keys off identity, not `matches()`, so a loosely-matching editor doesn't wrongly spare the target - Does nothing if the group referenced in context can't be resolved the setting is off Source PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328975

title: Voice Mode ambient glow redesign: verify it applies uniformly across the normal and Agents windows
content:
Tracking issue for the Voice Mode ambient glow redesign.

| PR | Scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328455 | The rim redesign across the chat inputs | Merged |
| https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 | Dictation mic glow uniformity | In review |

Voice Mode's ambient glow is currently a hardcoded blue/purple border plus box-shadow, applied identically on every surface. It reads as a focus ring rather than as a microphone being open, and it can't follow the theme.

The redesign replaces it with a single ambient light that says **who currently holds the floor**:

| State | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| `listening` | Audio-reactive interior rim, cool |
| `speaking` | The same rim, shifted warm |
| everything else | Nothing |

Colors derive from the theme accent (`chat.voiceGlowBaseColor`, defaulting to `focusBorder`) instead of being hardcoded, and high contrast themes opt out of the soft rim in favour of a solid line.

## Why this needs tracking

This is a UX change that touches every voice surface across two windows, so it needs verifying that it (a) doesn't regress anything around the chat input and (b) **applies uniformly** — the same glow, the same colors, the same states, everywhere voice appears.

## Surfaces in scope

| Window | Surface | Wiring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal window | Chat view (panel / sidebar / editor) | `chatViewPane.ts` |
| Agents window | Agent session chat view | `chatView.ts` |
| Agents window | Agent welcome / new chat view | `newChatVoice.ts` |
| Agents window | Agents voice widget | `agentsVoiceWidget.ts` |

## Verification

### Uniformity — the same treatment on every surface

For each of the four surfaces above:

- [ ] `listening` shows the cool rim; `speaking` shows the warm rim
- [ ] No glow in any other state (idle, processing, error, disconnected)
- [ ] `listening -> speaking` cross-fades rather than snapping
- [ ] The rim follows the input's corner radius on all four corners
- [ ] The mic glyph, voice pill and waveform all read the same accent as the rim

### No regressions around the chat input

- [ ] Send button is visible and clickable while the glow is active (it sits above the glow at `z-index: 12`)
- [ ] The full input toolbar stays available during voice — attachments, model picker, mode picker, settings
- [ ] The transcript overlay still renders correctly under the glow
- [ ] The glow is removed cleanly when voice stops, with no stale frame left behind
- [ ] No layout shift when the glow appears or disappears

### Theming

- [ ] Dark, light and high contrast (high contrast should show a solid line, not a soft rim)
- [ ] Glow follows a custom `chat.voiceGlowBaseColor`
- [ ] `chat.voiceListeningGlow` / `chat.voiceSpeakingGlow` pin individual states

### Accessibility and performance

- [ ] `workbench.reduceMotion: on` pins a still frame and swaps layers without cross-fading
- [ ] The OS-level reduced motion setting is honoured
- [ ] The animation frame loop only runs while a glow is actually rendered
- [ ] No new focusable or screen-reader-announced content (the glow is decorative)

## Dictation

Dictation originally picked up the shared accent token but painted it raw, while the rim paints a tuned version (hue nudged, saturation bounded, lightness pinned per theme) — so an open microphone looked different depending on which feature opened it.

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 fixes both halves: it moves that tuning into one shared helper both features resolve through, and mounts the actual rim on the microphone (scaled to the button) so it breathes like the chat input instead of pulsing.

- [ ] Dictation mic wears the actual rim (uneven, breathing light), not a uniform pulse
- [ ] Dictation mic glow matches the Voice Mode listening rim color, in light and dark
- [ ] Rim scales sensibly to the button and doesn't break into arcs or swamp the glyph
- [ ] Verified on all three dictation mics: chat execute toolbar, segmented voice-input pill, Agents window composer
- [ ] A theme pinning `chat.dictationActiveMicGlow` still wins, and is tuned the same way
- [ ] High contrast shows the same solid blue line as the listening rim

/cc @meganrogge




---

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 covers the dictation half: both features now resolve their color through one shared `resolveVoiceRimAccent` helper rather than two implementations that happened to agree, and dictation's high-contrast line matches the listening rim's. Verification checklist for it is in the Dictation section above.

title: Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes.
content:
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

Behaviour:
I have started to encounter this error since 1.126.0. Each time I open vs code it says Extension host terminated unexpectedly. I tried  `code --disable-extensions` and disable all the extensions but still got this error. I'm still using 1.125.0 as this version works fine. I'm in china and not sure if this is related. 


---

Can you share crash dump following https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Native-Crash-Issues#creating-a-crash-report to vscode-logs@microsoft.com

Thanks for replying. Just shared. I'll also share the report here. 

[reports.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30962975/reports.zip)

## AI Analysis
I analyzed all three dumps in the attached `reports.zip`. They have the same native crash signature:

```text
Process: node.mojom.NodeService (the local extension host utility process)
Crash reason: EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D)
Faulting module: C:\Windows\System32\ASProxy64.dll
Fault address: ASProxy64.dll + 0xc274
ASProxy64.dll version: 2.3.6.3

Stack prefix:
  ASProxy64.dll + 0xc274
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x1f4c2
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x65ec8
  ASProxy64.dll + 0xc506
  ASProxy64.dll + 0x1f8ad
  runtime.node
```

`ASProxy64.dll` is Astrill VPN's proxy/LSP DLL. It is injected into the extension-host process and executes the illegal instruction that terminates it. Because this is a system-wide Winsock provider, exiting Astrill or starting VS Code with `--disable-extensions` does not necessarily stop the DLL from loading.

This is the same faulting DLL, exception, and `+0xc274` stack signature previously investigated in #325035. In that report, properly cleaning up the Astrill/ASProxy installation resolved the crash.

The reported 1.125 -> 1.126 boundary does not coincide with an Electron target change: both releases use Electron target 42.3.0. The bundled Copilot extension and its native runtime did change between those releases (`@github/copilot` 1.0.61 -> 1.0.64-0). The dump returns from Astrill code into Copilot's `runtime.node`, so changed startup/network activity may have exposed the existing Astrill incompatibility, but the instruction that actually faults belongs to `ASProxy64.dll`.

Recommended remediation:

1. Update Astrill to its latest available version.
2. Properly unregister Astrill's LSP: hold **Ctrl**, open Astrill's **Help** menu, and select **Uninstall LSP**.
3. Log out of and close Astrill, then restart Windows.
4. If the LSP must remain installed, try excluding `Code.exe` using Astrill's Application Filter.
5. Avoid only deleting or renaming `ASProxy64.dll`; the Winsock provider should be properly unregistered to remove all traces safely.

No VS Code code change is indicated by these dumps. I am leaving this issue open for confirmation that unregistering/updating Astrill resolves it on the affected machine.

title: Space should not delete files on macOS when closing unsaved work
content: macOS has a convention that when closing with unsaved changes, the prompt is to save rather than to ask whether to save. E.g. this dialog in preview when you paste an image from the clipboard and then try to close it. The thing here is that there's no default button that you press with Spacebar or Enter to throw away your work. You can manually tab to the Delete button, click it or use Cmd+Delete to activate it, but you can't accidentally do this. The destructive action doesn't have a simple trigger. This should be the way that most apps work on macOS. I'm not sure what vscode should do here to do the right thing, but I'd assume doing a more native feeling dialog that does the right UX thing would be reasonable and not this: --- @joshka What do you mean by more native feeling dialog? That dialog you are showing is indeed a native macos dialog. Can you clarify what you expect to be different from the current experience? Apologies, as I know you already wrote a good amount of explanation but I didn't quite follow. The dialog is native in implementation (it calls all the right APIs), but native in expectation (it doesn't meet the expectations that are present in various macOS apps). I can see where the confusion about what I wrote comes in to play, but I meant the latter here. Make this feel like what macOS does when it has changes to a file and you quit or close the file - you get a save dialog, not a would you like to save dialog. Acceptance crieteria - pressing spacebar does not delete work - pressing enter does not delete work - pressing escape does not delete work - pressing cmd+delete deletes work. - button is red, says delete, is not focused @deepak1556 do we have the ability to make these types of dialogs? @joshka I see what you mean. I hesitate here a bit on the amount of information shown when a common use case is to use untitled files for scratch work and closing them is quite a tax with that large dialog. On the latest macOS and latest versions of VS Code: Enter, Spacebar, Escape DO NOT delete work. Enter triggers save, Escape dismisses the dialog but doesn't close the work. Spacebar does nothing. > Spacebar does nothing. 1. Cmd+N 2. type some text 3. Cmd+W 4. spacebar 5. dataloss of unsaved file The issue here is that there are various reasons that vscode may grab focus when and having an action which discards data selected by default is both a problem and has a better way of being displayed. The distinction is a save dialog vs a do you want to save dialog. That repro no longer works for me on latest macOS. I'm pretty sure it used to though. I'm still on sequoia - seems odd this would change @joshka and you are on the latest VS Code version 1.130? I saw some folks in another issue suggest that a specific VS Code version may have removed the default focusing of "Don't save" > @joshka and you are on the latest VS Code version 1.130? I saw some folks in another issue suggest that a specific VS Code version may have removed the default focusing of "Don't save" Problem still happens in 1.130: Cmd+N, asdf, Cmd+W, Space: Okay, from the information you've provided and what I read online, this does seem to be something they removed in Tahoe, so newer versions of macOS do not have this accidental loss of work issue. Keybinds are: Enter -> Save Escape -> Cancel CMD+D -> Delete > removed in Tahoe This feels like probably it's a reasonable 'wont fix' boundary. The root of this problem for me stemmed from something closing vscode with draft pending changes in a file that weren't recorded anywhere while I was typing in a text box in another app. The issue with that focus steal was that when I hit spacebar, vscode dropped the changes with no ability to restore. Classic footgun mechanic. I'm fine generally to note this as a broken, but fixed in the future and happy to close this out and take care to avoid it until then. Thanks for the diagnosis effort on this. Before I close it out, I'm trying to understand the behavior better with someone on the team who does have sequoia still. What's iteresting is in their case, nothing is selected by default either. Just fyi if it helps your situation, we have the option to use custom html dialogs which for me selecte "Save" by default. The setting is `window.dialogStyle` . Use `custom` Ah - that gives me a clue to the rest of the problem cause. I have keyboard navigation turned on in my macOS settings. I suspect this would likely still be a problem in Tahoe: Turning that off makes the button not selected by default. @joshka ah, that is helpful and does allow me to get focus selection. However, Cancel is the default selected entry when the dialog is shown. Confirming that with `Keyboard Navigation` turned on, I see `Dont Save` as the default. So it does seem something has changed between Sequoia and Tahoe. I don't currently plan to address this given it seems the OS is controlling this in some way and the latest version is doing what seems to be the desired behavior. Thank you @joshka for bearing with us on that. Codex response - I validated this based on actually watching and interacting with the noted test behaviors. I had two sessions one pointing at vscode and one at electron both with this issue as context and the idea about looking into exposing the destructive flag as possibly a thing as well as understanding why this is weird in sequoia. The root TLDR cause on this is vscode button order shuffling - don't save is the last button to be added, so it gets keyboard focus. --- I dug further into the native path. One useful distinction is that **Save is still the default button** here: Return activates Save. **Don't Save has keyboard focus**, so Space activates it when macOS Keyboard Navigation is enabled. VS Code currently changes the logical order `[Save, Don't Save, Cancel]` into the native insertion order `[Save, Cancel, Don't Save]`. Electron then creates an `NSAlert`, assigns Return and Escape using `defaultId`/`cancelId`, but otherwise leaves AppKit to choose the initial first responder. On Sequoia 15.7.7, an isolated AppKit test reproduced the result: that VS Code insertion order initially focuses Don't Save. Preserving `[Save, Don't Save, Cancel]` instead initially focuses Cancel, so removing VS Code's legacy macOS button shuffle appears to be the smallest immediate fix. Separately, Electron currently has no message-box option corresponding to `NSButton.hasDestructiveAction`. Testing that property with the existing VS Code order also moved initial focus from Don't Save to Cancel. Adding such an Electron option would be the more explicit long-term solution, including destructive appearance and AppKit semantics, but it isn't required for the narrow ordering fix. Verified in latest insiders: With Keyboard navigation ON, "Cancel" is the default selected now (does not delete the files). With Keyboard navigation OFF, "Save" is the default on "Enter". thanks for the fix - can confirm all good now in release version. I understand the sentiment, and this is arguably a sane default. Is there any way we could make this configurable though? I often keep various unsaved "scratch" documents and use keyboard navigation to close them quickly when e.g. "Closing all to the right". It's a shortcut I use multiple times a day and was frustrated to find gone. Ideally the keyboard shortcut for **Don't Save** should be `Cmd+Delete` and the button should be marked destructive (that's not wired through between Electron and macOS though) > Separately, Electron currently has no message-box option corresponding to NSButton.hasDestructiveAction. Testing that property with the existing VS Code order also moved initial focus from Don't Save to Cancel. Adding such an Electron option would be the more explicit long-term solution, including destructive appearance and AppKit semantics, but it isn't required for the narrow ordering fix. FWIW this issue being "fixed" feels like a regression to me. Actually I specifically enabled "Keyboard Navigation" in macOS settings to be able to have more options quickly reachable in dialogs (not just in vscode): Enter: save Escape: cancel Space: don't save A few days ago, default focus switched to "cancel" instead of "don't save". Now : Enter: save Escape: cancel Space: cancel => two quick keybindings for the cancel, while the third option is harder to reach. I think it is indeed important to prevent file removal by mistake for regular macOS config (it was already the case before this change, space did not delete the file). But if you enabled "Keyboard Navigation", that's because you want more things quickly doable with your keyboard. Yeah, I sort of miss it too at times - especially when I've made small edits to a file that I know is updated via a formatter / agentic change elsewhere. The muscle memory of close, discard is pretty ingrained and so it's definitely different. However I think the measure of whether it's good or not has to come from what harm does it prevent. It's pretty easy to see that there are circumstances where accidental data loss occurs. I'd easily prefer 99 more difficult interactions to 1 data loss scenario. Another evaluation lens might be to look for other macOS native apps (as opposed to electron stuff) that seems to do the right thing with dialogs when closing the app / a file. I suspect that you won't find many where spacebar is destructive. But the answer to this has a good technical path to solve your simple keystroke ideal here (which I want too). Implement hasDestructiveAction in electron, and add Cmd+Delete as the keyboard shortcut for don't save. Probably the latter can be done already. The former is not too hard either, but requires enough coordination of pieces that I didn't want to throw some LLM slop at this. > However I think the measure of whether it's good or not has to come from what harm does it prevent. It's a fine position but I don't believe it's definitive. My view of keyboard navigation in macOS is that Enter triggers the primary/blue thing of the dialog, Escape closes doing nothing, and Space trigger the first other option. The whole point of keyboard navigation is to have an extra alternative outlined. If you don't want keyboard navigation, you don't have to enable it. > Another evaluation lens might be to look for other macOS native apps (as opposed to electron stuff) that seems to do the right thing with dialogs when closing the app / a file. I suspect that you won't find many where spacebar is destructive. I just tried out SublimeText which is the other tabbed editor I have : The Pages/Numbers apps examples are not the same kind of dialog. If I press Enter in our dialog, then I get a similar one. And indeed the first alternative input is selected and space writes in it. But Space does not trigger cancel here either. Adding my voice to ask for making this configurable at least. It should be easy to close a scratch editor and dismiss its contents. `Cmd+W, Space` was perfect for that. I think this change is overly cautious and making a perfectly normal workflow unnecessarily complicated. Also, please keep in mind that in order for the space key to do anything in this situation, Keyboard navigation has to be turned on in the macOS system preferences as shown in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325273#issuecomment-5052743766, so this is automatically a power user feature.

title: Integrated terminal automatically sends 'Y' when terminating node batch script
content:
Thank you so much for looking into this 🙏 ! Issue Type: Bug ```console ~ > npm run concurrently \"script-1.js\" \"script-2.js\" ~ > [ type >> ctrl + c] ~ > Terminate batch job (Y/N)? Y (this character is automatically sent, but only terminates first script, putting remaining output in prompt on next line) ~ > [0] node script-name ~ > [type >> enter] ~ > y (character is still present, with spaces prepended) ~ > y : The term 'y' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program. Check the spelling of the name, or if a path was included, verify that the path is correct and try again. At line:1 char:1 ``` * The character y is never typed. * This does not happen in Windows Terminal. ctrl + c works as expected. VS Code version: Code 1.64.0 (5554b12acf27056905806867f251c859323ff7e9, 2022-02-03T04:22:20.678Z) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19044 Restricted Mode: No

Extensions (10) Extension|Author (truncated)|Version ---|---|--- es6-string-css|bas|0.1.0 python|ms-|2022.0.1786462952 vscode-pylance|ms-|2022.2.0 jupyter|ms-|2022.1.1001775990 remote-wsl|ms-|0.64.2 powershell|ms-|2021.12.0 LiveServer|rit|5.7.4 es6-string-html|Tob|2.12.0 vscode-todo-highlight|way|1.0.5 es6-string-javascript|zjc|1.0.1
A/B Experiments ``` vsliv368cf:30146710 vsreu685:30147344 python383:30185418 vspor879:30202332 vspor708:30202333 vspor363:30204092 pythonvspyl392cf:30425750 pythontb:30283811 pythonptprofiler:30281270 vshan820:30294714 vstes263cf:30335440 pythondataviewer:30285071 vscod805:30301674 pythonvspyt200:30340761 binariesv615:30325510 bridge0708:30335490 bridge0723:30353136 vsaa593cf:30376535 vsc1dst:30433059 pythonvs932:30410667 wslgetstartedc:30433508 vscop940:30404999 vsrem710:30416614 vscop841:30430977 ```
--- You can fix this by setting the value of terminate hatch job within terminal.integrated.autoReplies to null @meganrogge, Thank you so much! I should have checked if this was a setting first. Just curious - is this a new setting/behavior? Just started happening with 1.64. This is still a bug. This happens for me too. Every time I type `CTRL+C` it autoresponds `Y`. Now every time I type anything in the terminal after this, it writes Y after it: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43886029/152754656-df8d0083-a428-4ad5-8791-4dac52a0d12a.png) ```powershell Y : The term 'Y' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable progr am. Check the spelling of the name, or if a path was included, verify that the path is correct and t ry again. At line:1 char:1 + Y + ~ + CategoryInfo : ObjectNotFound: (Y:String) [], CommandNotFoundException + FullyQualifiedErrorId : CommandNotFoundException ``` If I type any command that gives a prompt, it stops autoresponding with `Y`. It also seems that writing git commands in the terminal somehow stops the `Y`autoresponse. Edit: Like like @meganrogge mentioned, adding ```json "terminal.integrated.autoReplies": { "Terminate batch job (Y/N)": null } ``` to settings.json will prevent this from happening. Note that this is just a workaround, since it does not fix the actual issue of `Y` being responded to any message, but rather disables the autoresponse alltogether I bet this is conpty reprinting causing duplicate responses 🤦 Updating to Windows 11 might workaround this as I've never hit this issue. The theory is that something running in the terminal is triggering conpty (the backend component) to reprint the screen which would re-output the match text. Thanks for the report, I'm going to disable it by default to be safe. We also had an idea for later on to allow the feature to be discovered intuitively when the user responds manually. How to configure for the batch job message is now called out in the docs: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2193314/152862499-049b261f-73a4-44c5-9d14-b2332a53fee7.png) > meganrogge, Thank you so much! I should have checked if this was a setting first. Just curious - is this a new setting/behavior? Just started happening with 1.64. This indeed is new with 1.64, see the [release notes](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_64#_automatic-replies) for details. I'm trying to use this to automatically enter Y when terminating a batch job. It is giving me an error after my next command though, because it enters "Y" again. This is what I have in settings.json: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26261118/153479033-99569eed-832d-4d13-b412-59f06b7cbe0d.png) And this is my terminal: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26261118/153479411-4e84bfbe-1cc1-4709-a31a-80b6d272d14f.png) I saw Windows 11 was mentioned above. Do I need to be on that in order to use this feature? Yes on older versions of Windows this is less reliable as the terminal emulation provided by Windows ends up reprinting the screen, causing the phrase to show up again. Shouldn't this be fixed for Windows 10 too though? It's still supported by Microsoft and VSCode, right? So is the conclusion just "Not supported you gotta disable it on Windows 10 yourself" and case closed? Doesn't seem right. Ok I see you disabled it by default in a merge request. So the state is now "this isn't supported on Windows 10"? How about this: Currently it seems to go "if (buffer.Contains(trigger)) send(reply);" So what if instead it goes "if (buffer.Contains(trigger) && !buffer.Contains(trigger+reply)) send(reply);" You know, just check if the line that was found already has a reply? Thanks for the reply. I don't think it is OK to leave it as is. I saw it in the release notes (https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_64#_automatic-replies) and spent way too much time trying to get it to work before finding this thread. Can it either be fixed to work with Windows 10 or update the docs to make it clear that Windows 11 is needed?

I think I know what's happening:

1. These machines are ones where GPU acceleration doesn't work and we fallback to the DOM
2. Webgl init throws [here](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/d81b25c3bf6c0e3352c175705f460aa39df6e374/addons/addon-webgl/src/WebglRenderer.ts#L101-L104) which disables it
3. But it doesn't appear that we clean up listeners created earlier, so [this listener](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/d81b25c3bf6c0e3352c175705f460aa39df6e374/addons/addon-webgl/src/WebglRenderer.ts#L92) ends up firing shortly afterwards which causes the texture atlas to get created and warmed up. This operating is either totally broken or impossibly slow with this setup which causes the problem.

So the fix I think is to make sure any listener in `WebglRenderer`'s ctor is disposed if it throws.

I think this was caused because we previously detected such systems and removed it as it was thought we no longer needed that check in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/236276. We may want to bring that back (@deepak1556?), but I believe the change above should fix the problem.

You can see the visual difference. Issue seems to be from `contextmenu` event being fired twice on an element that messes up the state managed by this extension. It got regressed with https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/44954 due to missing return after the first dispatch. title: add support in omni-chat to run vscode commands
content:
Adding to our initial LLM call which determines whether to route the request to a new session or to an existing one, we'd want to detect if a VS Code command can handle the request.

Then, we'd add a new looking mode where we display the command that's getting run with a 10 second time out to cancel it.

---

Sharing media and context from merged PR #330025 for verification:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf215eed-072e-40bb-925d-f5149b6e5896

## Summary

- add a first-stage command-vs-chat intent decision to omni-chat routing
- restrict command routing to a curated set of reversible built-in VS Code UI commands
- shortlist and classify commands using localized command titles only; command IDs are never sent to the model
- deterministically recognize common directives such as `toggle terminal`, `toggle panel`, and `change VS Code theme`
- show a 5-second `Running command X` review state with Run Now, Send to Chat, and Cancel actions
- focus the invoking workbench window before revalidating and executing the command
- preserve explicit new-session and pending voice-reply routing
- use a 5-second session-routing countdown, retaining 10 seconds for multi-root workspaces where folder selection may require more time

## Commands eligible for execution

Only the following currently enabled built-in commands are considered. All other built-in and extension commands continue through chat/session routing.

### Views and layout

- Focus Panel (`workbench.action.focusPanel`)
- Focus Primary Side Bar (`workbench.action.focusSideBar`)
- Focus Secondary Side Bar (`workbench.action.focusAuxiliaryBar`)
- Toggle Panel (`workbench.action.togglePanel`)
- Toggle Primary Side Bar (`workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility`)
- Toggle Secondary Side Bar (`workbench.action.toggleAuxiliaryBar`)
- Toggle Terminal (`workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal`)
- Toggle Zen Mode (`workbench.action.toggleZenMode`)
- Toggle Full Screen (`workbench.action.toggleFullScreen`)

### Pickers and settings

- Open Settings (`workbench.action.openSettings`)
- Open Keyboard Shortcuts (`workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings`)
- Quick Open (`workbench.action.quickOpen`)
- Show Command Palette (`workbench.action.showCommands`)
- Select Color Theme (`workbench.action.selectTheme`)
- Select File Icon Theme (`workbench.action.selectIconTheme`)
- Select Product Icon Theme (`workbench.action.selectProductIconTheme`)

Commands that edit files, format documents, run tasks or code, mutate source control, manage extensions or accounts, or come from extensions are intentionally excluded.

## Routing examples

Expected to enter command review:

- `toggle terminal`
- `toggle panel`
- `toggle sidebar`
- `open settings`
- `open keyboard shortcuts`
- `open command palette`
- `change VS Code theme`

Expected to continue to chat:

- `fix terminal toggling`
- `format this document`
- `run a task`
- `change VS Code theme in this extension`

## Voice Mode follow-up

The frontend displays and executes the selected command. Spoken `Running command X` acknowledgement requires corresponding voice-backend support so the utterance is not also routed into chat.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused `sessionRouter.test.ts` command filtering, deterministic phrase, and prompt tests
- focused `chatSessionRoutingController.test.ts` command review, original-window focus, and auto-run tests
- `git diff --check`

Source PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330025

title: `send_to_terminal` progress message repeats first question when accepting all defaults in interactive commands
content:
## Bug

When an interactive command like `npm init` is run and the user accepts all defaults via the `askQuestions` carousel, every `send_to_terminal` progress message displays the first question's text (e.g. "Package name?") instead of the correct question for each prompt.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session in default approvals mode
2. Ask the agent to run `npm init` in a terminal
3. The agent detects the interactive prompts and shows an `askQuestions` carousel with multiple questions (package name, version, description, entry point, etc.)
4. Accept all defaults by leaving every field empty and submitting the carousel
5. The agent sends each default answer via `send_to_terminal` (pressing Enter for each prompt)

## Expected Behavior

Each `send_to_terminal` progress message should show the corresponding question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: version?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: description?)
- …

## Actual Behavior

Every progress message repeats the first question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- …

## Cause

`_getQuestionContextForTerminal` matches the sent command text against carousel answer values to find the corresponding question. When all answers are identical (empty string for defaults), the loop iterates questions in order and always matches the first one.

## Fix

Use positional matching: count prior `send_to_terminal` tool invocations after the carousel in the response parts to determine the question index, rather than relying solely on answer-value matching.

title: Block auto-approval of file-write redirection to ~ and % paths
content:
Extends the file-write redirection guard to also block auto-approval when the destination path contains `~` (POSIX tilde expansion) or `%` (Windows env-var expansion), since neither `posix.isAbsolute` nor `win32.isAbsolute` classifies these as absolute paths.

Adds regression tests for both bash (`~/file.txt`, `%HOME%/file.txt`) and pwsh (`~\file.txt`, `%APPDATA%\file.txt`).

Tracking internal PR: devdiv-microsoft/vscode-private#43

title: Omni-chat folder routing
content:
We should add support for multi-root routing in omni-chat
- [ ] In a multi-root workspace, mention one folder explicitly in a prompt that creates a new session. Verify the session is created for that folder.
- [ ] Repeat with a file or resource associated with another folder and with a prompt related to an existing folder-scoped session. Verify the strongest relevant folder is selected.
We should add a **Change folder** action and an indicator of which folder was chosen as well



---

Implemented and validated as part of #326698, which is now merged into main. Omni multi-root routing selects new-session folders from attached resources, explicit folder mentions, related-session metadata, or the configured default, and the destination UI shows the selected folder with a Change Folder action.

Sharing media and context from merged PR #330024 for verification:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84913ee3-412a-4a1b-aea7-6ce01e6f1ac4

## Description

Omni already computed a workspace folder for new sessions, but its common new-session paths dispatched immediately. In multi-root workspaces this bypassed the destination panel, so users saw neither the selected folder nor a way to correct it before dispatch.

## Folder routing

For a new session in a multi-root workspace, Omni chooses the folder in this order:

1. **Explicit folder mention:** matches the prompt against a workspace folder's display name or final path segment. Matching is case-insensitive, treats spaces, dots, underscores, and hyphens equivalently, recognizes “VS Code” as “vscode”, ignores names shorter than three characters, and prefers the longest match.
2. **Attached resource:** uses the workspace folder containing the first attached file or resource that maps into the workspace.
3. **Related session:** uses the first model-ranked result with confidence of at least 0.35 whose working directory or repository metadata maps to a workspace folder. Working directory is checked before repository path, and nested matches prefer the deepest folder.
4. **Default folder:** uses the last folder selected for a new Agent Host session when it is still part of the workspace.
5. **Final fallback:** uses the first workspace folder.

The inferred destination is displayed as **New session in _folder_**. Its compact folder control opens an Agents-style searchable workspace menu anchored inside Omni. The menu lists every current workspace root with its full path and selected state, plus **Choose Folder…** for the native folder dialog and standalone working directories. Opening either picker pauses the countdown and closing or selecting resumes from the remaining time.

Standalone folders use the existing Agent Host trust boundary: before spawning, workspace roots request workspace trust and external folders request resource trust for the selected URI. Declining aborts the agent invocation.

The model picker renders in an adjacent transparent host above Omni, while the folder picker renders in a detached host to Omni's right. Neither picker resizes Omni. Omni's temporary local compose session also explicitly uses the Copilot Agent Host model pool, so the model picker shows the available targeted models instead of only **Auto**.

## Changes

- Route multi-root new sessions through the correctable destination panel.
- Show the inferred folder in a compact folder/chevron control before dispatch.
- List all workspace roots in an anchored, searchable, accessible folder menu.
- Add an Agents-style **Choose Folder…** action backed by the native folder dialog.
- Preserve the existing Agent Host workspace/resource trust gate for selected folders.
- Keep the model picker detached above Omni and open the folder picker to its right without resizing Omni.
- Use the Agent Host model pool for Omni's routing composer.
- Preserve automatic dispatch with the existing 10-second countdown and pause/resume behavior.
- Keep single-root new sessions on the immediate path.
- Add browser coverage for explicit folder inference, workspace selection, native folder selection, anchoring, filtering, and countdown behavior.

title: Agent response file summary includes repository changes made between turns
content: ## Reproduction 1. Install and launch the latest [VS Code Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/). 2. In PowerShell, create a local bare remote, a workspace clone, and one remote commit that the workspace has not pulled yet: ```powershell $root = Join-Path $env:TEMP "agent-turn-attribution-$([DateTimeOffset]::Now.ToUnixTimeSeconds())" $remote = Join-Path $root 'remote.git' $seed = Join-Path $root 'seed' $workspace = Join-Path $root 'workspace' New-Item -ItemType Directory $root | Out-Null git init --bare --initial-branch=main $remote git init -b main $seed 'base' | Set-Content (Join-Path $seed 'agent.txt') 'base' | Set-Content (Join-Path $seed 'external.txt') git -C $seed add agent.txt external.txt git -C $seed commit -m 'Initial files' git -C $seed remote add origin $remote git -C $seed push -u origin main git clone $remote $workspace Add-Content (Join-Path $seed 'external.txt') 'remote-change-to-pull' git -C $seed add external.txt git -C $seed commit -m 'Remote change to sync between agent turns' git -C $seed push code-insiders $workspace ``` At this point, `workspace` is one commit behind the remote `main` branch, but its working tree still contains the original `external.txt`. 3. Trust the folder, open Chat (`Ctrl+Alt+I`), select **Agent** mode, and set the session target to **Copilot**. 4. Send this prompt and approve the edit: ```text Edit agent.txt by appending exactly one new line containing first-agent-edit. Do not change any other file. After editing, stop. ``` 5. Verify that the first response reports **1 file changed, +1, -0**. 6. Between turns, advance the checkout entirely through the VS Code UI: 1. Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) and run **Git: Fetch** so VS Code discovers that the branch is behind. 2. Open Source Control (`Ctrl+Shift+G`). 3. Click **Sync Changes** (the circular-arrows action) and confirm if prompted. The sync performs a fast-forward pull. `external.txt` now contains `remote-change-to-pull`, while the first turn's change in `agent.txt` remains modified and uncommitted. 7. In the same chat, send this prompt and approve the edit: ```text Edit agent.txt by appending exactly one new line containing second-agent-edit. Do not change any other file. After editing, stop. ``` 8. Expand the second response's file-change summary. ## Actual result The second response includes `external.txt` and attributes the commit pulled by **Sync Changes** to the agent's second turn. With the example above, it reports **2 files changed, +2, -0** instead of the single line the agent added. The effect is much larger when Sync Changes, pull, merge, rebase, or checkout advances the repository substantially between turns. In one long-lived session, a response incorrectly reported **1030 files changed, +45890, -10554** even though that turn changed one CSS file. ## Expected result The second response should report only: - `agent.txt` - **1 file changed, +1, -0** The session-wide Changes view may correctly include both files; only the per-response summary should be scoped to changes made between the start and end of that agent turn. ## Additional context The issue also affects the Agents window because both surfaces consume the Agent Host server's per-turn changeset. The same problem can be triggered by other Git operations that advance or rewrite the checkout between turns, including pull, merge, rebase, and checkout. A fix is proposed in #329715. --- I cannot repro this @DonJayamanne Actually, what you see is the repro. I have updated steps to avoid manual edits, so using only VS Code UI now - here's the result: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f04a6f8d-1d8c-4d03-84b0-ce36948336d9)

title: Status bar style refresh asserts before part creation in the Agents window
content:
The Agents window repeatedly logs this assertion during startup:

```text
2026-08-11 08:33:39.074 [error] Assertion Failed: Argument is `undefined` or `null`.: Error: Assertion Failed: Argument is `undefined` or `null`.
    at NE (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:414:242)
    at Qi (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:414:1216)
    at Mlt.updateStyles (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:1414:72690)
    at Rxe.value (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:1414:66143)
    ...
    at wSi.registerDefaultConfigurations (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:462:74842)
    at R6e.processExperimentalSettings (.../out/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.js:4790:35997)
```

I found five occurrences across four recent Agents window renderer logs.

The stack resolves to `StatusbarPart.updateStyles()`, specifically `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`. The Agents window creates the shared status bar service but intentionally does not create/render the status bar part. During startup, experimental/default configuration registration fires `onDidChangeConfiguration`; the listener added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329701 calls `this.updateStyles()` before a container exists.

The root fix appears to be making this configuration-driven refresh lifecycle-safe. For example, `updateStyles()` can return while `getContainer()` is undefined. Normal status bar styling remains covered because `Part.create()` invokes `updateStyles()` after assigning the container, and later configuration changes still refresh it.

Introducing commit: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb55ea151447d7607654d7046a18b37d3dca4704

(Written by Copilot)

Fixed https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330323

title: Update ESLint to v10 (9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06)
content:
ESLint v9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06 and no longer receives fixes: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/ (see also https://eslint.org/version-support/). The repo currently pins `eslint@^9.36.0`.

Findings from running the v10.8 migration locally (`node build/eslint.ts` passes cleanly on the full repo afterwards):

- `typescript-eslint` / `@typescript-eslint/utils` support ESLint 10 since 8.56, so the current `^8.45.0` only needs a bump.
- `@stylistic/eslint-plugin-ts` v2 is a legacy package: the ts-specific plugin was merged into the unified `@stylistic/eslint-plugin`, whose v5 line supports ESLint 10 (rule ids change from `@stylistic/ts/semi` to `@stylistic/semi`).
- `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` declares ESLint 10 support as of v63.
- `eslint-plugin-import` is still on ESLint ≤9: the latest release (2.32.0, June 2025) relies on `context` APIs removed in v10, but works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()` from `@eslint/compat` (only `import/no-restricted-paths` is used here).
- `eslint-plugin-header` is unmaintained (last release Feb 2021, already needs the `meta.schema = false` workaround on v9) and also works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()`.
- The local rules (`.eslint-plugin-local`, `extensions/copilot/.eslintplugin`) need a mechanical port off `context.getFilename()` / `context.getSourceCode()`, which were removed in v10.
- v10 turns `/* eslint-env */` comments into errors; there is one inert instance in `test/unit/electron/renderer.js` (`no-undef` is not enabled).
- The newer `typescript-eslint` / `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` versions report a handful of new `prefer-optional-chain` / `check-param-names` findings, all easy to fix.

I'd like to open a PR with the migration if the team is open to it.


---

A PR is welcome.

title: Global Search result clicks do not expose selection/range to Custom Editor (webview) extensions
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.111.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.3.1

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install an extension that registers a `CustomTextEditorProvider` for `.md` files (e.g. [MEO](https://github.com/vadimmelnicuk/meo)).
2. Set the custom editor as the default for `.md` files via `workbench.editorAssociations`.
3. Use **Global Search** (`Cmd+Shift+F` / `Ctrl+Shift+F`) to search for a term present in a `.md` file.
4. Click a search result entry to open/navigate to the match.

Current Behavior:

The custom editor (webview) opens for the `.md` file, but the clicked match position is never surfaced to the extension via any stable API. The result is that the custom editor has no reliable way to scroll to or highlight the clicked search match - a fundamental navigation expectation that works automatically for native text editors.


Expected Behavior:

When a Global Search result is clicked and the target file resolves to a Custom Editor, VS Code should surface the target match position to the extension via at least one of:
- The `options` parameter of `resolveCustomTextEditor` (e.g. a `selection` or `range` field, analogous to `TextDocumentShowOptions.selection`).
- A dedicated event or message posted to the webview containing the target range.
- A stable public API (analogous to `vscode.window.activeTextEditor`) that exposes the requested scroll/reveal target for the active custom editor.

Use Case:

Extensions that replace the native text editor with a rich webview UI (WYSIWYG markdown editors, hex editors, visual data editors, notebook-like interfaces) need to respond to navigation requests from Global Search, Go to Definition, and similar VS Code surfaces. Without a range-passing mechanism, these editors cannot provide the expected "jump to match" behaviour, making Global Search effectively non-functional for files owned by a custom editor.

title: Support Custom Protocol Links (e.g. zotero://) in Markdown Preview and Notebook
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

**Description:**

I am a VS Code user who frequently works with academic references managed by Zotero. Zotero generates custom protocol links (e.g. `zotero://select/library/items/XXXXXX`) that allow users to jump directly to specific items in their local Zotero library.

**Problem:**
Currently, when I insert a `zotero://` link in a markdown file or a Jupyter Notebook markdown cell, the link is rendered in the preview, but clicking it does not trigger the system protocol handler. Instead, nothing happens or an error occurs. In the editor, I can use workarounds (such as selecting the link and using a custom extension), but in the markdown preview or notebook rendered view, there is no way to activate these links.

**Use Case:**
- Academic note-taking and research workflows often require quick access to local reference managers like Zotero.
- Many users embed `zotero://` links in markdown notes, notebooks, or documentation to streamline their citation workflow.
- Supporting clickable custom protocol links would greatly improve productivity and integration with local tools.

**Feature Request:**
- Allow custom protocol links (such as `zotero://`, `org-protocol://`, etc.) to be clickable in markdown preview and notebook rendered cells.
- When clicked, VS Code should invoke the system protocol handler, similar to how browsers handle these links.
- Optionally, provide a setting to enable/disable this feature for security reasons.

**Additional Context:**
- This feature is already supported in browsers and some local applications.
- The lack of support in VS Code limits the integration of local reference managers and other custom tools.

**My Attempts to Solve This (with AI Assistance):**
I have tried to solve this problem with the help of GitHub Copilot (AI assistant). We explored all possible technical paths, including:
- Developing a custom VS Code extension to intercept link clicks in markdown preview or notebook renderers.
- Creating a Webview-based custom preview to handle protocol links.
- Using scripts or context menus in the editor to trigger links.

However, all these approaches are either blocked by VS Code’s API limitations or require significant effort and compromise on user experience (such as abandoning the native preview). After thorough exploration, I found that none of these solutions are cost-effective or practical for end users. Native support from the VS Code team would be the most efficient and user-friendly solution.

**Thank you for considering this feature!**


---

Following extension allows you to hover over "zotero://" links in the editor window (so not in the preview window) and open the link. Far from perfect, but a workaround for now: [Zotero link opener (on GitHub)](https://github.com/jorisvanzundert/zotero-link-opener)

title: Outline drag-and-drop and layer visibility
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

While it's easy to manage and sort classes, private/public methods, and functions when a project is small, it becomes very difficult to keep all the context in mind as the codebase grows.

Currently, editor-folding is one tool we have for this(though it can be buggy, as I've reported in issue #310842). However, a much more convenient option already exists conceptually:  **OUTLINE** view.

Since VS Code already builds an AST to map out the document symbols, could we add some **drag-and-drop** functionality to the Outline panel? I would be incredibly powerful to rearrange classes, functions, and methods directly in the Outline view for languages that support this coding style (moving symbol in the Outline would automatically cut and paste the corresponding block in the editor).

Additionally, the Outline view currently expands fully every time a window or file loads, forcing me to manually collapse things to getan overview. It would be wonderful to introduce visibility toggles/layers, such as:

- `Classes Layer`/`Global Layer` - Collapses everything to show only top-level classes and global functions.
- `Method Layer` - Unfolds classes but keeps their internal methods/properties collapsed.

This would drastically improve code navigation and refactoring efficiency for large files.

title: Add a "Restart VS Code" button in the UI
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

my request is comade with copilot since im not a native english speaker:

Dear Microsoft / VS Code team,
I would like to suggest adding a dedicated "Restart VS Code" button to the user interface.
Currently, VS Code prompts users to restart after updates, but there is no easy, always-available way to manually trigger a full restart when needed. Having a restart option would be useful in cases where users want to ensure that the session is fully reset (e.g., after changing settings, extensions, or troubleshooting issues).
Proposed solution

Add a "Restart VS Code" button accessible from the UI
A natural location could be under the Settings gear menu or the Command Palette
The action should:

Fully restart the application
Preserve workspace state similar to normal restarts



Why this would be helpful

Ensures a clean session without leftover state
Improves troubleshooting experience
Provides consistency (restart is already prompted after updates)
Makes the feature more discoverable for users who are not familiar with command-based workflows

Additional context
This is a small quality-of-life improvement, but it would be a nice and practical addition to the overall developer experience.

---

From Command Palette (F1) you can run `Developer: Reload Window`

> From Command Palette (F1) you can run `Developer: Reload Window`

> Makes the feature more discoverable for users who are not familiar with command-based workflows

This is exactly my point: more and more non‑power users are joining the community, and they often prefer UI-based interactions over command-based ones.
Having a visible restart button would make this functionality more discoverable and accessible. Similar to how many users prefer the built-in Git UI over the terminal—even if the terminal is faster—because it lowers the barrier to entry.
So this would be a small but valuable quality-of-life improvement.

I feel like `Developer: Reload Window` serves the need already - for troubleshooting needs etc.
For other scenarios, I'd be curious if you have more specifics on why you believe restart is needed - if there are bugs where state is not cleared when expected, we should fix those bugs.

title: Start Menu pinned tile becomes invisible (transparent) after every auto-update on   Windows
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

Steps to Reproduce:
  Environment:
  - OS: Windows 10 22H2 (19045)
  - VS Code version: 1.100+ (happens every update, across multiple versions)
  - Install type: System Installer, custom path E:\Program Files\ide\Microsoft VS Code

  Steps to reproduce:
  1. Pin VS Code to the Start menu (tile area). The tile displays correctly.
  2. Wait for an auto-update, or trigger one via "Check for Updates".
  3. After the update completes, open the Start menu.

  Observed behavior:
  The pinned VS Code tile becomes completely invisible/transparent (not a white square —
  truly empty, nothing renders). The shortcut itself is intact, Code.exe exists at the
  correct path, and clicking the invisible tile still launches VS Code normally.

  Workaround that works every time:
  Right-click the blank tile → "Unpin from Start" → re-pin from Code.exe. Or, right-click
  the .lnk shortcut → Properties → Shortcut tab → "Change Icon..." → OK → Apply (without
  actually changing the icon). Both restore the tile immediately.

  What has been ruled out:
  - ❌ Shortcut target path is NOT broken — TargetPath still points to correct Code.exe
  and IconLocation is Code.exe,0
  - ❌ No _ (underscore) subfolder issue — Code.exe is directly in install directory, not
  moved
  - ❌ Icon cache corruption — ie4uinit.exe -show alone doesn't always fix it; restarting
  StartMenuExperienceHost.exe does
  - ❌ Not specific to custom install path — the Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml and its
  referenced hash-named PNG folder are both intact post-update



  Possible root cause (AI-generated analysis):
  The root cause appears to be that VS Code's Inno Setup-based updater replaces Code.exe
  in-place during the update but does not call SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, ...) or
  ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache after the file replacement. Windows' Start menu tile host
  process (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe) holds a cached rendering of the old Code.exe's
  icon resources in memory. Because the file path hasn't changed, Windows does not
  automatically invalidate the cache, and the stale cached data fails to map to the new
  binary's icon resources — resulting in the tile rendering nothing (invisible rather than
  a white fallback).

  Additionally, Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml references icon PNGs via a hash-named
  subfolder (e.g. <hash>\resources\app\resources\win32\code_150x150.png). Even though the
  manifest is updated to the new hash during installation, if StartMenuExperienceHost.exe
  has cached the manifest content from before the update, it may still reference the old
  (now-deleted) hash folder path. This would also cause a transparent tile.

  Suggested fix:
  In the Inno Setup installer script, add a post-install step:

  [Code]
  procedure CurStepChanged(CurStep: TSetupStep);
  begin
    if CurStep = ssPostInstall then
      SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, SHCNF_IDLIST, 0, 0);
  end;

  Or in the [Run] section:

  [Run]
  Filename: "{cmd}"; Parameters: "/c ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache"; Flags: runhidden


---

Thanks for creating this issue! It looks like you may be using an old version of VS Code; the latest stable release is 1.125.1. Please try upgrading to the latest version and checking whether this issue remains.

Happy Coding!

We want to use custom agents for some requirements but are unable to use inbuilt browser tools because workbench.browser.enableChatTools shows as disabled. This setting is managed by organization and due to "Preview Feature" policy disabled on Github.com by organization, we are unable to use this tool.

Due to this, we have no choice but to use playwright mcp separately which bloats the context window. This feature was launched in March. When is the plan to move it from an "Experimental" to "Stable" featureset. I would assume once its no longer under Experimental feature, it should be controllable on User Level instead of org level. 

Its a useful feature and I believe it makes no sense to still keep it an experimental state or leave it to be managed by org policy.

---

Any updates on this?

Hi @kycutler , are there any near future plans to transition it to stable?

Hi @akashyxp, thanks for opening this -- the tools have been stable for a while, so we've gone ahead and progressed them out of experimental state. They will still have their own separate policy that can be configured by organizations, but they won't be blanket disabled by the preview features policy.

Thanks a lot for this. Much appreciated

title: GitHub Copilot Chat extension is sometimes present in extension list, sometimes not
content:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.121.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.5 (25F71)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run the command `code --list-extensions`
2. Observe whether `github.copilot-chat` is present in the list

It seems to change from day-to-day or week-to-week. My theory is that with every new VS Code release, it ships with the most-up-to-date version of the extension bundled (and therefore is not present in the list), but the extension later receives an update over the bundled one (and becomes present in the list). I haven't thoroughly tested this theory, but it went from present to not present when I updated to the latest release (1.121.0). My guess is that it was introduced in 1.116.0, [when this extension became built-in](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_116#_github-copilot-is-now-builtin).

All I know is that I use that command to regularly sync [my VS Code extensions](https://github.com/jaminthorns/environment/blob/main/config/code/extensions/extensions), and `github.copilot-chat`'s presence in the list keeps changing. If my theory is correct, then I suppose that either:

- Any bundled extension should be excluded from `code --list-extensions`, regardless of whether it's been updated over the bundled version.
- All bundled extensions that are updatable should be included in `code --list-extensions`.

My guess is that the first would be easier to implement. Regardless, I'd just like for things to be consistent again.

---

This extension is now only present in the built-in list (`@builtin` search filter), so this no longer seems to be an issue.

title: fix: guard statusbar updateStyles against pre-create config change (fixes #330262)
content:
### Summary The status bar throws `Assertion Failed: Argument is undefined or null.` at startup on Mac, Windows and Linux (v1.133.0-insider, 326 users). `StatusbarPart.updateStyles()` calls `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`, but the newly-added configuration-change listener invokes `updateStyles()` while default configurations are still being registered — before the part's container (`this.parent`/`this.element`) exists — so the assertion fires. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#330262 Recommended reviewer: `@hawkticehurst` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`eb55ea15`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb55ea151447d7607654d7046a18b37d3dca4704) | | Author | `@hawkticehurst` | | PR | #329701 | | Message | Restore theme colors in Modern UI shell (#329701) | | Why | This commit added `this.updateStyles();` inside the `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener (statusbarPart.ts:228). That listener can fire during early startup — while `registerDefaultConfigurations` runs — before `Part.create()` sets `this.parent`, so `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())` in `updateStyles()` receives `undefined` and throws. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reg as ConfigurationRegistry participant Cfg as ConfigurationService participant Listener as StatusbarPart config listener participant Update as StatusbarPart.updateStyles participant Assert as assertReturnsDefined Reg->>Cfg: registerDefaultConfigurations (startup) Cfg->>Listener: onDidChangeConfiguration(MODERN_UI) Note over Listener: Root cause:
calls updateStyles() before
the part container exists Listener->>Update: updateStyles() Update->>Assert: assertReturnsDefined(getContainer()) Note over Assert: Error thrown:
Argument is undefined or null ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarPart.ts` | crash site | L697 (from stack): `const container = assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer());` | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarPart.ts` | root cause | L225-L230: config listener calls `this.updateStyles()` unconditionally, before `create()` sets the container | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/part.ts` | context | L78-L85: `create()` sets `this.parent` then calls `updateStyles()`; `getContainer()` returns `this.parent` | ### Repro Steps The error is timing-dependent (fires only when a `MODERN_UI` default-configuration change is delivered before the status bar part is created during startup): 1. Launch VS Code (insider) so that experimental/default settings are registered during startup. 2. When `registerDefaultConfigurations` triggers an `onDidChangeConfiguration` event affecting `workbench.modernUI` before the workbench finishes creating the status bar part, `updateStyles()` runs with no container. 3. The assertion `Argument is undefined or null` is thrown from `assertReturnsDefined(this.getContainer())`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`statusbarPart.ts`): guard the newly-added `updateStyles()` call in the config-change listener with `if (this.element)`, so it only runs once the part has been created into a container. This fixes the problem at its source — the producer of the premature call — rather than at the crash site. The part already models the "not yet created" state explicitly elsewhere (e.g. `addEntry` checks `if (!this.element)` at L268), so this guard is consistent with existing lifecycle handling. When the part is later created, `Part.create()` calls `updateStyles()` (part.ts:85), so no style update is lost. **Alternatives considered:** - Relaxing `updateStyles()` to use `this.getContainer()?...` throughout, which would weaken the invariant for the other legitimate callers that expect a container to exist and mask genuine ordering bugs. - Wrapping the call in try/catch, which would hide the error from telemetry instead of preventing the invalid call — rejected because errors must continue to surface. ### Recommended Owner `@hawkticehurst` — author of the culprit commit #329701 which introduced the `updateStyles()` call in the config listener, and the active owner of the Modern UI shell status bar styling work. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/31504179817) · opus48 · 449.9 AIC · ⌖ 11.1 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/statusbar-updatestyles-guard-330262-e366edab9c857081`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/statusbar-updatestyles-guard-330262-e366edab9c857081). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-08-11T15:17:08.991Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. title: fix: enrich truncated IPC object deserialize error (fixes #330263)
content:
### Summary

Telemetry bucket `112c22ba-c8f9-9d2c-1f93-9f46466fb2ac` reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` thrown from `JSON.parse` inside `deserialize()` in `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`, running in the agent host utility process (`agentHostMain.js`) while decoding an inbound IPC message delivered over a MessagePort. The message payload arrives truncated: the binary framing declares an object of N bytes, but fewer than N bytes are present, so `JSON.parse` on a partial/empty string fails with a context-free error that gives triage no way to see where the corruption happened. New in `1.133.0-insider` (`5a36a9c6`); not present in the `1.132.0` baseline (`df53daab`), matching the introduction of the Agent Host Protocol-over-IPC (MessagePort) plumbing.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#330263
Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312`

### Culprit Commit

Ancestry could not be git-verified in this environment (blobless checkout, credentials stripped after checkout, so `git show <hash>` / `merge-base --is-ancestor` fail on on-demand object fetch). Within the `1.132.0` to `1.133.0-insider` regression window, the agent-host MessagePort transport that routes these IPC messages was introduced/reworked by:

- `63a042819ddd4deaffd45ac84dc176d1f00bb49a` — "agentHost: use AHP for local connections" (routes local renderer traffic through the Agent Host Protocol over MessagePort) — Connor Peet (`@connor4312`).

This is the most likely producer of the new truncated-frame path; the crash surfaces in the shared `deserialize()` utility rather than in the transport commit itself.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[MessagePortMain message event - native Electron layer] -->|e.data possibly truncated| B[Protocol.onMessage ipc.mp.ts:21-26 VSBuffer.wrap or alloc 0]
    B --> C[ChannelServer.onRawMessage / onBuffer ipc.ts]
    C --> D[deserialize reader ipc.ts:304]
    D -->|DataType.Object| E[readIntVQL yields length N]
    E --> F[reader.read N - BufferReader.slice returns fewer than N bytes, NO error on underflow]
    F --> G[JSON.parse of partial string ipc.ts:322]
    G -->|SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input| H[telemetry bucket 112c22ba]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts` — `deserialize()` `DataType.Object` case (crash site and where the truncation first becomes observable). `BufferReader.read()` (lines 217-221) slices without erroring on underflow, so a short buffer silently yields a partial string.

### Repro Steps

Deterministic user repro is not available (the truncation originates in the native MessagePort/utility-process boundary during agent host connect/disconnect, not in reproducible TS logic). Observed across Windows/Mac/Linux, 44 users, on `1.133.0-insider`. Conceptually: deliver a MessagePort frame to the agent host whose binary object header declares more bytes than the payload actually contains (e.g. a partial/racing frame during agent host teardown) and `deserialize` will attempt `JSON.parse` on a truncated string.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`, `deserialize()` `DataType.Object` case (the bypass site is `ipc.ts:322`, where `reader.read(N)` can return fewer than N bytes without error because `BufferReader.read` slices without bounds-checking). Before calling `JSON.parse`, read the declared length N and the actual buffer, and if the buffer is shorter than declared, throw an enriched error naming the expected vs. received byte counts. This follows the cross-process-error principle: enrich the error with diagnostic context, do not swallow it. The error is still thrown and still reaches the telemetry pipeline, but the new bucket will carry actionable framing information (`expected N, received M`) instead of an opaque `Unexpected end of JSON input`, letting the transport owner see truncation is occurring and where. This does not add a `try/catch`, does not remove any `logService.error`, and does not coerce the bad value to a benign default — the corrupt frame is still rejected loudly.

**Alternatives considered**
- Wrap `JSON.parse` in `try/catch` and return `undefined`/empty object — rejected: swallows a real cross-process corruption, hides the producer, and breaks the telemetry signal that surfaced the bug.
- Drop empty/short messages at the producer in `Protocol.onMessage` (`ipc.mp.ts`) — rejected as the primary fix: the true producer is the native MessagePort layer (not visible in TS), the exact truncation condition isn't reconstructable from source, and silently dropping frames there would mask the corruption for every channel without diagnostics. Enriching at the deserialization boundary keeps the signal while making it diagnosable for whichever transport is at fault.

### Recommended Owner

`@connor4312` — authored the 1.133 Agent Host Protocol-over-MessagePort IPC plumbing (`63a042819dd`, "agentHost: use AHP for local connections") that introduced the new transport path in which this error appears.
